Theorem
[Strong maximum principle]1. ch2:2.2\group chapter-2 Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0027 ↗ gt.thm2.1 If $\Delta u\geq 0$ in a domain $\Omega $ and $u$ attains its supremum at an interior point, then $u$ is constant. The analogous assertion holds for $\Delta u\leq 0$ and an interior minimum. Thus a nonconstant harmonic function has no interior extremum.
Proof

↗ gt.thm2.1 \sketch The set where $u$ equals its maximum is relatively closed. The ball mean inequality from Theorem 1 shows that this set contains a neighborhood of each of its points, hence is also relatively open. Connectedness finishes the proof; replace $u$ by $-u$ for minima.

□
